narration.transcript: Want the look of old timber beams without the weight? Meet Heritage Timber by Ekena Millwork. Each beam is cast from real, weathered timber, so it looks solid, even up close. A 5.5-inch beam, 12 feet long, weighs about 18 pounds. One person can lift it. It slides over a wood block with standard household tools, and it's hollow so it can hide wiring. And unlike solid wood, it resists warping and cracking with less upkeep. Pick from six hand-stained finishes or primed, eight cross-section sizes, in lengths from four to 24 feet. It's in stock and usually ships in three to five business days. Order a sample and see it in your own light.

findings.source: raw/flat-BMSTS3C00600X0600X144KB.json: weight 18.00 and shippingWeight 18.0000 (shipping box 6×6×145 in)
findings.what: H21 rests on the record's 'weight' field. In all 16 Heritage records (flat-BMSTS3C*.json), 'weight' is exactly the same as 'shippingWeight': 8/8, 12/12, 18/18, 25/25, 36/36, 40/40 and so on. The shipping dimensions are the box (6×6×145 in for this beam). So the 18 lb is most likely the packed shipping weight, not the beam's own weight. The card hedges with 'Listed weight', but the spoken line says the beam 'weighs about eighteen pounds', and the compare table states '18 lb' outright. This is v6 e9 with new evidence. The builder declined it for Brody to decide.
findings.fix: Brody / the product team: confirm the net beam weight. Until then, either change the line in build/script-v7.json#weight to 'ships at about eighteen pounds' (the eyebrow reads 'SHIPS AT' and the compare cell says 'about 18 lb shipped'), or keep the wording and change H21's source to 'shipping weight 18 lb'.
